```python
    SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak,
```

## 2.1 DOCX Generation with Node.js `docx` Package

**Date:** May 2026
**Source:** Conversation `57692f44`
**Context:** Generates the Bayyinah Audit Framework as a Word document
matching the Munafiq Protocol's academic formatting. Shows the transition
from ad-hoc PDF scripting to modular document composition.

```javascript
// Generate reformatted Bayyinah Audit Framework matching Munafiq Protocol style
const fs = require('fs');
const {
  Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, AlignmentType, HeadingLevel,
  PageBreak, LevelFormat, TabStopType, TabStopPosition, BorderStyle,
  Table, TableRow, TableCell, WidthType, ShadingType, PageNumber, Footer
} = require('docx');

// ---- Style helpers ----
const BODY_FONT = "Times New Roman";
const HEADING_FONT = "Times New Roman";

function p(text, opts = {}) {
  return new Paragraph({
    alignment: opts.alignment || AlignmentType.JUSTIFIED,
    spacing: { after: opts.after !== undefined ? opts.after : 120, line: 276 },
    indent: opts.indent,
    children: [new TextRun({
      text,
      font: BODY_FONT,
      size: opts.size || 22,
      bold: opts.bold || false,
      italics: opts.italics || false,
    })],
  });
}

function pRuns(runs, opts = {}) {
  return new Paragraph({
    alignment: opts.alignment || AlignmentType.JUSTIFIED,
    spacing: { after: opts.after !== undefined ? opts.after : 120, line: 276 },
    indent: opts.indent,
    children: runs,
  });
}

function r(text, opts = {}) {
  return new TextRun({
    text,
    font: BODY_FONT,
    size: opts.size || 22,
    bold: opts.bold || false,
    italics: opts.italics || false,
  });
}

function center(text, opts = {}) {
  return p(text, { ...opts, alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER });
}

function h1(text) {
  return new Paragraph({
    spacing: { before: 360, after: 180, line: 276 },
    keepNext: true,
    children: [new TextRun({
      text, font: HEADING_FONT, size: 28, bold: true
    })],
  });
}

function h2(text) {
  return new Paragraph({
    spacing: { before: 240, after: 120, line: 276 },
    keepNext: true,
    children: [new TextRun({
      text, font: HEADING_FONT, size: 24, bold: true
    })],
  });
}

function fig(text) {
  return new Paragraph({
    alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER,
    spacing: { before: 120, after: 120 },
    border: {
      top: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 4, color: "888888" },
      bottom: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 4, color: "888888" },
      left: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 4, color: "888888" },
      right: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 4, color: "888888" },
    },
    children: [new TextRun({
      text, font: BODY_FONT, size: 20, italics: true, color: "555555"
    })],
  });
}

function ref(text) {
  return new Paragraph({
    alignment: AlignmentType.JUSTIFIED,
    spacing: { after: 80, line: 276 },
    indent: { left: 360, hanging: 360 },
    children: [new TextRun({ text, font: BODY_FONT, size: 20 })],
  });
}

// Build document with centered title page, abstract, justified body,
// numbered sections, references with hanging indent, AI contribution
const children = [];
children.push(new Paragraph({
  spacing: { before: 1200 }, children: [new TextRun("")]
}));
children.push(new Paragraph({
  alignment: AlignmentType.CENTER,
  spacing: { after: 200 },
  children: [new TextRun({
    text: "The Bayyinah Audit Framework",
    font: HEADING_FONT, size: 36, bold: true
  })],
}));
// [Full document content building continues through abstract,
//  methodology, panel composition, verdict architecture,
//  AI contribution statement, and references]
```

## 3.1 Pandoc + XeLaTeX Academic Paper Rendering Script

**Date:** July 2026
**Source:** Conversation `c02852de`
**Context:** Renders the at-Taleem (Defence of the Dissertation) paper.
The script handles Arabic glyphs and transliteration diacriticals through
XeLaTeX with DejaVu Serif.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# render_pdf.sh <input.md> <output.pdf>
pandoc "$1" -o "$2" \
  --pdf-engine=xelatex \
  -f markdown-smart \
  -V documentclass=article \
  -V mainfont="DejaVu Serif" \
  -V monofont="DejaVu Sans Mono" \
  -V geometry:margin=1in \
  -V fontsize=11pt \
  -V linestretch=1.15 \
  -V colorlinks=true -V linkcolor=black -V urlcolor=black -V citecolor=black \
  -H <(printf '%s\n' \
      '\usepackage{etoolbox}' \
      '\usepackage{booktabs}' \
      '\usepackage{longtable}' \
      '\AtBeginEnvironment{longtable}{\footnotesize}' \
      '\setlength{\emergencystretch}{3em}' \
      '\usepackage{sectsty}\allsectionsfont{\sffamily\bfseries}' )
```

## 4.1 CI v0.2 Code-Generated Register Architecture

**Date:** August 11, 2026
**Source:** Conversation `b744718e` and related XZ Protocol sessions
**Context:** Deterministic register generator that replaced LLM-authored
prose with computed output. Produces defect register text from a JSON
findings index, boundary lists, and terminal lines. Core of the
Crystallographic Ijaz (CI) v0.2 architecture — the first code in the
account that generates text with a provenance trail embedded in its
structure.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""xz_protocol_register_gen.py -- CI v0.2 Code-Generated Register."""
import json

def generate_register(index_path: str, version: str) -> str:
    with open(index_path) as f:
        index = json.load(f)
    groups = index["convergence_groups"]
    noted = index.get("unique_findings_noted", [])
    round_num = index["round"]
    sev_order = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2, "INFORMATIONAL": 3}
    closed = [g for g in groups if g["disposition"] == "CLOSED"]
    closed.sort(key=lambda g: (
        sev_order.get(g["triage_severity"], 9), g["group_id"]
    ))
    noted_groups = [g for g in groups
                    if g["disposition"] in ("NOTED", "DEFERRED")]
    correction_base = ord('v')
    correction_idx = 0
    lines = []
    lines.append(
        f"R{round_num} defect register disposition "
        f"(from R{round_num} five-seat audit, {len(closed)} items):"
    )
    for item_num, group in enumerate(closed, 1):
        ids = group["finding_ids"]
        n = group["seat_count"]
        sev = group["triage_severity"]
        defect = group["defect_class"]
        disp = group["disposition"]
        repair = group.get("repair_type", "correction")
        id_list = " / ".join(ids)
        bracket = f"[{n}-seat convergence: {id_list}]"
        if repair == "correction":
            letter = chr(correction_base + correction_idx)
            correction_idx += 1
            disp_text = (
                f"{disp} via append-only correction (b{letter})"
            )
        elif repair == "gate":
            gate_id = group.get("gate_id", "[10x]")
            disp_text = f"{disp} via gate {gate_id}"
        elif repair == "architecture":
            disp_text = (
                f"{disp} via CI v0.2 code-generated register architecture"
            )
        else:
            disp_text = disp
        adj = ""
        if "triage_adjudication" in group:
            adj = f" Adjudication: {group['triage_adjudication']}"
        line = (
            f"({item_num}) {bracket} {sev} {disp_text}: "
            f"{defect}.{adj} [COMPUTED: generate_register]"
        )
        lines.append(line)
    if noted_groups or noted:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            f"NOTED (non-converging or deferred, "
            f"{len(noted_groups) + len(noted)} items):"
        )
        for g in noted_groups:
            ids = " / ".join(g["finding_ids"])
            lines.append(
                f"- [{g['seat_count']}-seat: {ids}] "
                f"{g['triage_severity']}: {g['defect_class']}. "
                f"Disposition: {g['disposition']}."
                f"{' ' + g.get('note', '') if g.get('note') else ''} "
                f"[COMPUTED: generate_register]"
            )
        for n in noted:
            lines.append(
                f"- [{n['finding_id']}] {n['source_severity']}: "
                f"{n['substance']}. Disposition: {n['disposition']}."
                f"{' ' + n.get('note', '') if n.get('note') else ''} "
                f"[COMPUTED: generate_register]"
            )
    return "\n".join(lines)

def generate_boundary_list(boundaries_path: str) -> str:
    with open(boundaries_path) as f:
        boundaries = json.load(f)
    items = boundaries["items"]
    count = len(items)
    item_texts = [item["text"] for item in items]
    joined = ", ".join(item_texts)
    return (
        f"Disclosed standing boundaries -- {count} items: {joined} "
        f"[ENUMERATED: {count} items] "
        f"[COMPUTED: generate_boundary_list]"
    )

def generate_terminal_line(version: str) -> str:
    return f"*End of XZ Protocol v{version} draft candidate.*"
```

## 4.2 R30 Probe Battery Framework — Adversarial Mutation Harness

**Date:** August 17, 2026
**Source:** XZ Protocol audit sessions
**Context:** The probe battery framework provides `probe()`, `sub()`,
`restore()`, `reseal()`, `build()` functions for systematically testing
which build gates catch which mutations. This is adversarial code — code
whose purpose is to attack other code to find its weaknesses.

```python
import hashlib, subprocess, shutil, os, sys, json
BASE = "/home/claude/xz/work"
P = "/home/claude/xz/probe"

def dig(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(p, 'rb').read()).hexdigest()[:12]

def restore():
    for f in os.listdir(P):
        os.remove(os.path.join(P, f))
    for f in os.listdir(BASE):
        sp = os.path.join(BASE, f)
        if os.path.isfile(sp):
            shutil.copy(sp, P)

def reseal():
    names = sorted([
        f for f in os.listdir(P)
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(P, f))
        and f != "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"
    ])
    with open(os.path.join(P, "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"), "w") as fh:
        for n in names:
            h = hashlib.sha256(
                open(os.path.join(P, n), 'rb').read()
            ).hexdigest()
            fh.write(f"{h}  {n}\n")

def build():
    r = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "build.py"], cwd=P,
        capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    fails = [
        l for l in r.stdout.split("\n")
        if l.strip().startswith("FAIL:")
    ]
    return r.returncode, len(fails), fails

def probe(name, fn, expect):
    restore()
    before = {
        f: dig(os.path.join(P, f))
        for f in os.listdir(P)
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(P, f))
    }
    fn()
    after = {
        f: dig(os.path.join(P, f))
        for f in os.listdir(P)
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(P, f))
    }
    landed = before != after
    if not landed:
        print(f"{name}: VOID -- mutation did not land")
        return
    reseal()
    rc, nf, fails = build()
    verdict = ("BUILD PASSED" if rc == 0
               else f"BUILD FAILED ({nf} fail-checks)")
    flag = ("FALSE-PASS" if (rc == 0 and expect == "catch")
            else ("caught" if rc != 0 else "passed"))
    print(f"{name}: mutation LANDED | {verdict} | {flag}")
    for f in fails[:4]:
        print("      ", f.strip())

def sub(fn, old, new, count=1):
    p = os.path.join(P, fn)
    s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
    assert s.count(old) >= 1, f"pattern absent: {old[:60]}"
    open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(
        s.replace(old, new, count)
    )
```

## 4.3 Q11 Self-Consistent Forgery Probe — The Critical Vulnerability

**Date:** August 17, 2026
**Source:** XZ Protocol audit sessions
**Context:** This is the most consequential code in the XZ Protocol era.
It proves that the seal chain is not tamper-evident against an adversary
who controls the build instrument: mutate a sealed entry, regenerate all
seals, and derive PRIOR_HISTORY via build.py's own `derive_prior_history()`
→ **BUILD PASSED**. This finding — that syntactic integrity verification
is insufficient when the verifier is compromised — is the conceptual
ancestor of FATIMA's insistence on structural (bond-graph) verification
above Shannon's boundary.

```python
import hashlib, subprocess, shutil, os, sys, re, importlib.util
BASE = "/home/claude/xz74/work"
P = "/home/claude/xz74/probe"
shutil.rmtree(P, ignore_errors=True)
os.makedirs(P)
for f in os.listdir(BASE):
    sp = os.path.join(BASE, f)
    if os.path.isfile(sp):
        shutil.copy(sp, P)

pp = os.path.join(P, "xz_protocol_v0_74.md")
s = open(pp, encoding='utf-8').read()
before = hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()

# THE MUTATION: change a sealed protocol entry
s = s.replace(
    "*End of XZ Protocol v0.63 draft candidate.*",
    "*End of XZ Protocol v0.99 draft candidate.*", 1
)
open(pp, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
assert hashlib.sha256(
    open(pp, 'rb').read()
).hexdigest() != before

# REGENERATE ALL SEALS from the mutated document
def regen_seals():
    t = open(pp, encoding='utf-8').read()
    s27 = t[t.find("## 27."):]
    out = []
    for m in re.finditer(
        r'(- \*\*v0\.(\d+)[^*]*\*\*.*?)'
        r'(?=\n- \*\*v0\.|\n\*Provenance|\Z)',
        s27, re.DOTALL
    ):
        out.append(
            f"{hashlib.sha256(m.group(1).strip().encode()).hexdigest()}"
            f"  ENTRY_v0.{m.group(2)}"
        )
    prov = s27.find("*Provenance and review status.*")
    out.append(
        f"{hashlib.sha256(s27[:prov].strip().encode()).hexdigest()}"
        f"  FULL_SECTION_27"
    )
    return out

hist = os.path.join(P, "HISTORY.sha256")
oldp = [
    l.strip() for l in open(hist)
    if l.strip().startswith("PRIOR_HISTORY")
]
open(hist, "w").write(
    "\n".join(regen_seals() + oldp) + "\n"
)

# USE THE BUILD SYSTEM'S OWN FUNCTION to derive
# the "correct" PRIOR_HISTORY for the forged document
src = open(os.path.join(P, "build.py")).read()
ns = {"__name__": "notmain"}
exec(compile(src, "build.py", "exec"), ns)
proto = open(pp, encoding='utf-8').read()
hl = [l.strip() for l in open(hist) if l.strip()]
derived = ns["derive_prior_history"](proto, hl)
open(hist, "w").write(
    "\n".join(regen_seals() + [f"PRIOR_HISTORY {derived}"])
    + "\n"
)

# RESEAL THE MANIFEST
names = sorted([
    f for f in os.listdir(P)
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(P, f))
    and f != "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"
])
with open(os.path.join(P, "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"), "w") as fh:
    for n in names:
        fh.write(
            f"{hashlib.sha256(open(os.path.join(P, n), 'rb').read()).hexdigest()}"
            f"  {n}\n"
        )

# THE RESULT: BUILD PASSED on a forged document
r = subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "build.py"], cwd=P,
    capture_output=True, text=True
)
# returncode == 0 — the forgery is undetectable
```

```python
WORK = "/home/claude/xz50/work"

def sha(text):

def sha_file(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, 'rb').read()).hexdigest()

def reseal_entry(proto_path, version_num):
    """Reseal a single ENTRY in Section 27."""
    text = open(proto_path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    s27 = text[text.find("## 27."):]
    pattern = (
        rf'(- \*\*v0\.{version_num}[^*]*\*\*.*?)'
        rf'(?=\n- \*\*v0\.|\n\*Provenance|\Z)'
    )
    m = re.search(pattern, s27, re.DOTALL)
    return sha(m.group(1).strip())

def reseal_full_s27(proto_path):
    """Reseal FULL_SECTION_27."""
    text = open(proto_path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    s27 = text[text.find("## 27."):]
    prov = s27.find("*Provenance and review status.*")
    return sha(s27[:prov].strip())

def update_packet_sums(work_dir):
    """Regenerate PACKET_SHA256SUMS."""
    names = sorted([
        f for f in os.listdir(work_dir)
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(work_dir, f))
        and f != "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"
    ])
    with open(os.path.join(work_dir, "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"), "w") as fh:
        for n in names:
            h = sha_file(os.path.join(work_dir, n))
            fh.write(f"{h}  {n}\n")

# M1: Duplicate seal line (HISTORY cardinality gate bypass)
# M2: False [DIFF-VERIFIED] tag injection (ungated enzyme)
# M3: NC-prefix finding ID (regex bypass)
# M4: Arbitrary HISTORY line injection (format bypass)
# M5: Bare (E) token in shadow zone below [10b]
# M6: Whitespace-only entry mutation (seal mismatch)
```

## 4.5 Digest Cascade / PACKET_SHA256SUMS Regeneration

**Date:** August 11, 2026
**Source:** XZ Protocol audit sessions
**Context:** Multi-pass digest propagation for v0.57 builds. Handles
the circular dependency: code files → manifest → trust roots → body
references → PACKET_SHA256SUMS. Shows the complete file set and
cascade resolution logic.

```python
import hashlib, json, os

CODE_MODULES = sorted([
    "xz_protocol_kernel.py",
    "xz_protocol_condition_a.py",

    "test_xz_protocol_kernel.py",
    "test_xz_protocol_condition_a.py",
])

ALL_CODE = sorted(set(CODE_MODULES + TEST_SUITES))

def sha256_file(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(65536), b''):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()

# Pass 1: compute code file digests for manifest

for f in ALL_CODE:
    d = sha256_file(f)
    manifest_lines += f"{d}  {f}\n"

    manifest_lines.encode()
).hexdigest()

# Pass 2: update trust roots with manifest digest

    json.dump(tr, f, indent=2)
    f.write("\n")

# Pass 3: recompute all file digests for PACKET_SHA256SUMS
all_files = sorted([
    f for f in os.listdir(".")
    if os.path.isfile(f) and f != "PACKET_SHA256SUMS"
])
with open("PACKET_SHA256SUMS", "w") as fh:
    for fn in all_files:
        h = sha256_file(fn)
        fh.write(f"{h}  {fn}\n")

# Pass 4: rebuild HISTORY.sha256 seal chain
```

## 5.1 Hurst Exponent R/S Analysis with Monte Carlo Permutation Testing

**Date:** August 2026
**Source:** Conversation `34c876d2`
**Context:** R/S rescaled-range Hurst estimation per Cross-Text Thesis
v1.1 Sec 2.2. Tests whether the severity trajectory of XZ Protocol
amendment entries shows long-range dependence (H > 0.5). Includes
2000-iteration Monte Carlo permutation test and bootstrap CI.

```python
import re, numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260803)

def rs_hurst(x, min_n=4, max_cap=64):
    """R/S rescaled-range Hurst per Cross-Text Thesis v1.1 Sec 2.2:
    subseries sizes 4..min(N/2,64); log-log regression of mean R/S on n."""
    x = np.asarray(x, float); N = len(x)
    sizes = [n for n in range(min_n, min(N//2, max_cap)+1)]
    logn, logrs = [], []
    for n in sizes:
        k = N // n
        vals = []
        for i in range(k):
            s = x[i*n:(i+1)*n]
            m = s.mean()
            dev = np.cumsum(s - m)
            R = dev.max() - dev.min()
            S = s.std(ddof=0)
            if S > 0 and R > 0:
                vals.append(R / S)
        if vals:
            logn.append(np.log(n))
            logrs.append(np.log(np.mean(vals)))
    if len(logn) < 3:
        return None, 0
    H, _ = np.polyfit(logn, logrs, 1)
    return H, len(logn)

def mc(x, iters=2000):
    obs, _ = rs_hurst(x)
    null = []
    y = np.array(x, float)
    for _ in range(iters):
        rng.shuffle(y)
        h, _ = rs_hurst(y)
        if h is not None:
            null.append(h)
    null = np.array(null)
    p = (np.sum(null >= obs) + 1) / (len(null) + 1)
    return obs, null, p

# --- Series 1: ordinal severity trajectory ---
txt = open('xz_protocol_v0_37.md').read()
sec = txt[txt.index('## 27. Amendment record'):]
entries = re.split(r'\n- \*\*v0\.', sec)[1:]
SEVMAP = {'INFO': 0, 'LOW': 1, 'MEDIUM': 2, 'HIGH': 3, 'CRITICAL': 4}
sev, lens = [], []
for e in entries:
    if not re.match(r'\d+', e):
        continue
    best = 0
    for s, v in SEVMAP.items():
        if s != 'INFO' and re.search(r'\b' + s + r'\b', e):
            best = max(best, v)
    sev.append(best)
    lens.append(len(e))

for name, series in [("severity-ordinal", sev), ("entry-length", lens)]:
    obs, null, p = mc(series)
    lo, hi = np.percentile(null, [2.5, 97.5])
    print(f"\n=== {name} (N={len(series)}) ===")
    print(f"  H_obs        = {obs:.4f}")
    print(f"  shuffled H   = {null.mean():.4f}  "
          f"(null 95% CI [{lo:.4f}, {hi:.4f}])")
    print(f"  p (H>=obs)   = {p:.4f}   [2000 MC shuffles]")
    # bootstrap CI on H itself
    bs = []
    a = np.array(series, float)
    for _ in range(2000):
        idx = np.sort(rng.integers(0, len(a), len(a)))
        h, _ = rs_hurst(a[idx])
        if h is not None:
            bs.append(h)
    bs = np.array(bs)
    print(f"  bootstrap H 95% CI = "
          f"[{np.percentile(bs, 2.5):.4f}, "
          f"{np.percentile(bs, 97.5):.4f}]  "
          f"width={np.percentile(bs, 97.5) - np.percentile(bs, 2.5):.4f}")
```

## 5.2 Fractal Dimension Box-Counting in Base-3 Symbolic Space

**Date:** August 2026
**Source:** Conversation `34c876d2`
**Context:** Computes box-counting fractal dimension of the XZ Protocol
kernel's decision regions in base-3 ultrametric space. Imports and uses
the kernel's own `TruthValue`, `ConjunctVector`, and `evaluate_kernel`
— one of the few code specimens that operates on another piece of code
in the account as its *mathematical object*.

```python
import itertools, math, numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/home/claude/pkt')
from xz_protocol_kernel import (
    TruthValue as T, ConjunctVector, evaluate_kernel,
    generate_exhaustive_vectors, KernelDecision
)

vecs = generate_exhaustive_vectors()
sym = {T.TRUE: 'T', T.FALSE: 'F', T.UNKNOWN: 'U'}
regions = defaultdict(list)
for v in vecs:
    d = evaluate_kernel(v).decision
    regions[d.value].append(
        ''.join(sym[x] for x in v.as_dict().values())
    )

print("=== KERNEL DECISION REGIONS (3^5 = 243 states) ===")
for k, s in sorted(regions.items()):
    print(f"  {k:<14} |S| = {len(s):>3}   "
          f"measure = {len(s)/243:.4f}")

def box_dim(S, L=5, b=3):
    """Box-counting dimension in base-3 symbolic ultrametric space.
    D_k = log N(k) / (k log b).  D = 1 for the full space."""
    rows = []
    for k in range(1, L + 1):
        N = len(set(x[:k] for x in S))
        rows.append((k, b**-k, N, math.log(N) / (k * math.log(b))))
    return rows

for name in ['ALLOW', 'DENY_UNKNOWN', 'DENY_FALSE']:
    S = regions[name]
    rows = box_dim(S)
    print(f"\n  {name}  (|S|={len(S)}, measure={len(S)/243:.4f})")
    for k, eps, N, D in rows:
        print(f"    k={k}  eps={eps:.5f}  N(eps)={N:>3}  D_k={D:.4f}")
    print(f"    --> D_box ≈ {rows[-1][3]:.4f}")
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the Multi-Timeline Structural Honesty Methodology PDF."""

from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.lib.units import inch
from reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet, ParagraphStyle
from reportlab.lib.colors import HexColor
from reportlab.lib.enums import TA_CENTER, TA_JUSTIFY, TA_LEFT
from reportlab.platypus import (
    SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak,
    Table, TableStyle, KeepTogether, HRFlowable
)

WIDTH, HEIGHT = letter
MARGIN = 0.9 * inch

# Colour system — more refined than Era I
DARK = HexColor("#1a1a2e")
ACCENT = HexColor("#16213e")
GOLD = HexColor("#c4a35a")
MID = HexColor("#444444")
LIGHT_BG = HexColor("#f5f5f0")

styles = getSampleStyleSheet()

styles.add(ParagraphStyle(
    "DocTitle", parent=styles["Title"], fontSize=22, leading=28,
    textColor=DARK, spaceAfter=6, alignment=TA_CENTER,
    fontName="Helvetica-Bold"))

styles.add(ParagraphStyle(
    "Body", parent=styles["Normal"], fontSize=9.5, leading=13,
    textColor=HexColor("#222222"), spaceAfter=8,
    alignment=TA_JUSTIFY, fontName="Helvetica"))

styles.add(ParagraphStyle(
    "TableHead", parent=styles["Normal"], fontSize=8.5, leading=11,
    textColor=HexColor("#ffffff"), fontName="Helvetica-Bold"))

def make_table(headers, rows, col_widths=None):
    """Create a styled table — reusable builder pattern."""
    data = [[Paragraph(h, styles["TableHead"]) for h in headers]]
    for row in rows:
        data.append([
            Paragraph(str(c), styles["TableCell"]) for c in row
        ])
    if not col_widths:
        col_widths = [
            ((WIDTH - 2*MARGIN) / len(headers))] * len(headers)
    t = Table(data, colWidths=col_widths, repeatRows=1)
    t.setStyle(TableStyle([
        ("BACKGROUND", (0, 0), (-1, 0), ACCENT),
        ("TEXTCOLOR", (0, 0), (-1, 0), HexColor("#ffffff")),
        ("GRID", (0, 0), (-1, -1), 0.5, HexColor("#cccccc")),
        ("ROWBACKGROUNDS", (0, 1), (-1, -1),
         [HexColor("#ffffff"), LIGHT_BG]),
    ]))
    return t

# [12 content sections: title, TOC, central empirical result,
#  defect migration tables, framework analysis, CI trajectory,
#  irreducible floor, asymptotic barrier, multi-timeline,
#  dimensional verification, practical protocol, conclusions]
```

## 6.1 Atom — The Indivisible Semantic Unit

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/core/atom.py`)
**Context:** An Atom is to FATIMA what a byte is to Shannon: the
smallest unit that carries meaning. But unlike a byte, an Atom is
defined by its content, its structural relationships (bonds), and
its holographic shard. The docstring invokes the Names.

```python
"""
Atom — the indivisible semantic unit of a FATIMA document.

An Atom is to FATIMA what a byte is to Shannon: the smallest unit
that carries meaning.  But unlike a byte, an Atom is not defined by
its bits alone.  It is defined by its content, its structural
relationships (bonds) to other atoms, and its holographic shard —
a compressed encoding of a sufficient cross-section of the entire
bond graph, so that the meaning of the whole document can be
reconstructed from any k-of-n atoms.

This mirrors the architecture of the Names: each Name is a
self-contained unit, but each Name also *contains the whole*
(the holographic property established in The Most Beautiful Names).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional


@dataclass
class Atom:
    """A semantic unit in a FATIMA document."""

    atom_id: str
    content: str
    content_type: str = "proposition"
    content_hash: str = ""
    semantic_hash: str = ""
    bond_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    holographic_shard: bytes = b""
    shard_threshold: int = 0
    position: int = 0

    _VALID_TYPES = frozenset({
        "proposition",   # a claim or statement
        "definition",    # defines a term or concept
        "evidence",      # supports or demonstrates a claim
        "claim",         # an assertion to be supported
        "reference",     # points to an external source
        "metadata",      # structural/bibliographic information
        "invocation",    # Bismillah or similar sacred opening
    })

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.content_type not in self._VALID_TYPES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid content_type '{self.content_type}'. "
                f"Must be one of: {sorted(self._VALID_TYPES)}"
            )
        if not self.content_hash:
            self.content_hash = self._compute_content_hash()

    def _compute_content_hash(self) -> str:
        """SHA-256 of the content — Level 1 syntactic integrity."""
        return hashlib.sha256(
            self.content.encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()

    def compute_semantic_hash(self) -> str:
        """SHA-256 of content + bond IDs + shard — Level 2+.

        This captures the atom's position in the meaning-structure:
        the same content with different bonds has a different semantic
        hash, because its *meaning in context* is different.

        This is the mechanism by which Property 4 (Meaning-Integrity)
        operates: altering the bonds while preserving the content
        changes the semantic hash, making the distortion detectable.
        """
        material = (
            self.content + "|"
            + ",".join(sorted(self.bond_ids)) + "|"
            + self.holographic_shard.hex()
        )
        h = hashlib.sha256(material.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        self.semantic_hash = h
        return h

    def verify_syntactic(self) -> bool:
        """Level 1: has the content been altered?"""
        return self.content_hash == self._compute_content_hash()

    @property
    def has_shard(self) -> bool:
        return len(self.holographic_shard) > 0

    @property
    def structural_weight(self) -> int:
        """Number of bonds. Per NC-P2, losing a high-weight atom
        degrades confidence more than losing a low-weight atom."""
        return len(self.bond_ids)
```

## 6.2 Bond — Typed Semantic Relationship

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/core/bond.py`)
**Context:** The bond type taxonomy mirrors the relationships between
the Names of Allah: ar-Rahman DEFINES mercy, al-Adl QUALIFIES
ar-Rahman, each Name DEPENDS_ON every other, and the selective
suppression of any Name CONTRADICTS the holographic property.

```python
"""
Bond — typed semantic relationship between atoms.

A Bond encodes the *meaning-level* relationship between two semantic
units.  The bond graph is the structure that crosses Shannon's
boundary: syntactic integrity cannot detect the alteration of a bond,
but structural verification can.
"""

import enum
import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional


class BondType(enum.Enum):
    """Typed semantic relationships between atoms.

    The taxonomy mirrors the relationships observable between the
    Names of Allah: ar-Rahman DEFINES mercy, al-Adl QUALIFIES
    ar-Rahman, each Name DEPENDS_ON every other, and the selective
    suppression of any Name CONTRADICTS the holographic property.
    """
    DEFINES = "DEFINES"
    SUPPORTS = "SUPPORTS"
    CONTRADICTS = "CONTRADICTS"
    REFERENCES = "REFERENCES"
    DEPENDS_ON = "DEPENDS_ON"
    IMPLIES = "IMPLIES"
    ELABORATES = "ELABORATES"
    QUALIFIES = "QUALIFIES"

    @property
    def is_structural(self) -> bool:
        """Whether this bond type carries structural load.

        Structural bonds are load-bearing: their removal changes
        the meaning.  Non-structural bonds enrich meaning but
        their removal degrades rather than distorts.

        This maps to Property 3 (Tawhidic Unity): removing a
        structural bond breaks the unity; removing a non-structural
        bond is detectable but does not necessarily break
        reconstruction.
        """
        return self in (
            BondType.DEFINES,
            BondType.DEPENDS_ON,
            BondType.IMPLIES,
            BondType.CONTRADICTS,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Bond:
    """An immutable, typed semantic relationship between two atoms."""

    source_id: str
    target_id: str
    bond_type: BondType
    weight: float = 1.0
    rationale: str = ""

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not (0.0 < self.weight <= 1.0):
            raise ValueError(f"Weight must be in (0.0, 1.0]")
        if self.source_id == self.target_id:
            raise ValueError("Cannot bond an atom to itself")

    @property
    def bond_id(self) -> str:
        """Deterministic ID from source, target, type."""
        raw = (
            f"{self.source_id}:{self.target_id}:"
            f"{self.bond_type.value}"
        )
        return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]

    def reciprocal_type(self) -> Optional[BondType]:
        """Expected reciprocal bond type, if any.

        If A DEFINES B, then B DEPENDS_ON A.
        Contradiction is symmetric.
        """
        reciprocals = {
            BondType.DEFINES: BondType.DEPENDS_ON,
            BondType.DEPENDS_ON: BondType.DEFINES,
            BondType.IMPLIES: BondType.DEPENDS_ON,
            BondType.CONTRADICTS: BondType.CONTRADICTS,
            BondType.SUPPORTS: None,
            BondType.REFERENCES: None,
            BondType.ELABORATES: None,
            BondType.QUALIFIES: None,
        }
        return reciprocals.get(self.bond_type)
```

## 6.3 GF(2^8) Holographic Encoding — Crossing Shannon's Boundary

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/core/encoding.py`)
**Context:** The centrepiece. Adapts Shamir's Secret Sharing (1979) to
distribute the bond graph across atoms as holographic shards. The "secret"
is not a scalar — it is the serialised meaning-structure of the entire
document. 528 lines. Uses GF(2^8) arithmetic with generator element 3,
irreducible polynomial 0x11B (the AES polynomial), a precomputed 256×256
multiplication table for vectorised NumPy operations, and Lagrange
interpolation for reconstruction.

```python
"""
Holographic encoding — threshold distribution of the bond graph.

This module implements FATIMA Property 1 (Holographic Redundancy):
any sufficient cross-section of k-of-n atoms reconstructs the
complete bond graph.

The field is GF(2^8) — the same field used by Reed-Solomon codes
and AES, making the implementation well-studied.
"""

import json, os, zlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
import numpy as np


# --- GF(2^8) arithmetic ---
# Irreducible polynomial: x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 = 0x11B
# Generator element: 3 (x+1), primitive — generates all 255 nonzero

_GF_EXP = [0] * 512  # anti-log table
_GF_LOG = [0] * 256  # log table

def _gf_mul_raw(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Multiply in GF(2^8) via shift-and-XOR.
    Used only during table initialisation."""
    result = 0
    while b:
        if b & 1:
            result ^= a
        a <<= 1
        if a & 0x100:
            a ^= 0x11B
        b >>= 1
    return result

def _init_gf_tables() -> None:
    """Precompute log and anti-log tables using generator 3."""
    x = 1
    for i in range(255):
        _GF_EXP[i] = x
        _GF_LOG[x] = i
        x = _gf_mul_raw(x, 3)
    for i in range(255, 512):
        _GF_EXP[i] = _GF_EXP[i - 255]

_init_gf_tables()

# Full 256×256 multiplication table — 256 KB, fits in L2 cache
_GF_MUL_TABLE = np.zeros((256, 256), dtype=np.uint8)
for _a in range(256):
    for _b in range(256):
        if _a == 0 or _b == 0:
            _GF_MUL_TABLE[_a, _b] = 0
        else:
            _GF_MUL_TABLE[_a, _b] = _GF_EXP[
                _GF_LOG[_a] + _GF_LOG[_b]
            ]

def gf_mul(a, b):
    if a == 0 or b == 0: return 0
    return _GF_EXP[_GF_LOG[a] + _GF_LOG[b]]

def gf_div(a, b):
    if b == 0: raise ZeroDivisionError
    if a == 0: return 0
    return _GF_EXP[(_GF_LOG[a] - _GF_LOG[b]) % 255]


def _vectorised_lagrange_decode(shard_matrix, basis):
    """Recover all secret bytes via vectorised GF(2^8) dot product.

    Using the 256×256 multiplication table turns this into
    array indexing + XOR reduction — no Python-level loops.

    For a 250-atom molecule with k=125, this reduces ~200M
    Python-level GF operations to ~125 NumPy vectorised lookups.
    """
    k, num_bytes = shard_matrix.shape
    result = np.zeros(num_bytes, dtype=np.uint8)
    for i in range(k):
        b = int(basis[i])
        if b == 0: continue
        products = _GF_MUL_TABLE[b][shard_matrix[i]]
        result ^= products  # GF(2^8) addition is XOR
    return result


def encode_holographic(bond_graph_json, atom_ids, threshold):
    """Distribute the bond graph across atoms as holographic shards."""
    n = len(atom_ids)
    data = zlib.compress(bond_graph_json.encode("utf-8"), level=9)
    degree = threshold - 1
    shards = {aid: bytearray() for aid in atom_ids}
    for byte_val in data:
        poly = _make_polynomial(byte_val, degree)
        for i, aid in enumerate(atom_ids):
            x = i + 1  # evaluation points 1..n (never 0)
            shards[aid].append(_eval_polynomial(poly, x))
    return {aid: bytes(s) for aid, s in shards.items()}


def decode_holographic(shards, atom_ids_used, threshold, all_ids):
    """Reconstruct from k-of-n shards via vectorised Lagrange."""
    selected = atom_ids_used[:threshold]
    point_map = {aid: i + 1 for i, aid in enumerate(all_ids)}
    x_coords = np.array(
        [point_map[aid] for aid in selected], dtype=np.uint8
    )
    basis = _compute_lagrange_basis(x_coords)
    shard_matrix = np.array(
        [np.frombuffer(shards[aid], dtype=np.uint8)
         for aid in selected],
        dtype=np.uint8,
    )
    recovered = bytes(_vectorised_lagrange_decode(shard_matrix, basis))
    return zlib.decompress(recovered).decode("utf-8")
```

## 6.4 Molecule — The Bond Graph Architecture

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/core/molecule.py`)
**Context:** 448 lines. The Molecule is the unit at which all five
FATIMA properties are evaluated. It implements graph connectivity,
reciprocal bond verification, dangling bond detection, and
structural fingerprinting via SHA-256 of the bond graph.

```python
"""
Molecule — a document as a molecular structure with a bond graph.

The Molecule is the unit at which the five FATIMA properties are
evaluated:

  P1  Holographic Redundancy
  P2  Fitrah-Alignment
  P3  Tawhidic Unity
  P4  Meaning-Integrity
  P5  Authenticity via Structural Coherence

Trust degradation (NC-P2): if atoms are lost, trust degrades
monotonically — it never silently increases.
"""

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class Molecule:
    molecule_id: str
    title: str = ""
    atoms: dict[str, Atom] = field(default_factory=dict)
    bonds: dict[str, Bond] = field(default_factory=dict)
    bond_graph_hash: str = ""

    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the bond graph is connected.
        An unconnected molecule violates Tawhidic Unity."""
        if not self.atoms: return True
        adj = self.adjacency()
        start = next(iter(self.atoms))
        visited = set()
        stack = [start]
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            if node in visited: continue
            visited.add(node)
            stack.extend(adj.get(node, set()) - visited)
        return len(visited) == len(self.atoms)

    def dangling_bonds(self) -> list[Bond]:
        """Bonds referencing atoms not in the molecule.
        Evidence of tampering — Tawhidic Unity violation."""
        return [
            b for b in self.bonds.values()
            if b.source_id not in self.atoms
            or b.target_id not in self.atoms
        ]

    def compute_bond_graph_hash(self) -> str:
        """SHA-256 of the serialised bond graph.
        The structural fingerprint of the document's meaning."""
        bond_strings = sorted(
            f"{b.source_id}:{b.target_id}:"
            f"{b.bond_type.value}:{b.weight}"
            for b in self.bonds.values()
        )
        material = "\n".join(bond_strings)
        self.bond_graph_hash = hashlib.sha256(
            material.encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()
        return self.bond_graph_hash
```

## 6.5 Level 3: Holographic Verification

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/verification/holographic.py`)
**Context:** Sampling-based holographic verification. Tests whether
k-of-n subsets reconstruct the bond graph. Implements the NC-P2
principle: insufficient atoms → UNKNOWN (insufficient evidence),
not VIOLATED (we cannot prove violation without evidence of what
was lost). This three-valued epistemic distinction — VERIFIED /
UNKNOWN / VIOLATED — is the formal response to the Q11 forgery
finding from Era IV.

```python
"""
Level 3: Holographic Verification — reconstruction from cross-sections.

Trust degradation (NC-P2): if some atoms have lost their shards,
confidence is reduced proportionally.  If the count drops below k,
the verdict is UNKNOWN, not VIOLATED.
"""

from math import comb
import random
from itertools import combinations

def verify_holographic(molecule, sample_size=20, seed=None):
    """Level 3: verify holographic redundancy."""
    all_ids = [a.atom_id for a in molecule.atoms_by_position()]
    atoms_with_shards = [
        aid for aid in all_ids if molecule.atoms[aid].has_shard
    ]
    threshold = molecule.atoms[atoms_with_shards[0]].shard_threshold

    if len(atoms_with_shards) < threshold:
        # NC-P2: insufficient atoms → UNKNOWN, not VIOLATED
        return VerificationReport(
            verdict=Verdict.UNKNOWN,
            confidence=len(atoms_with_shards) / len(all_ids),
            violations=(
                f"Only {len(atoms_with_shards)} shards, "
                f"threshold is {threshold}",
            ),
        )

    # Full reconstruction
    ok, msg = verify_holographic_reconstruction(molecule)
    if not ok:
        return VerificationReport(verdict=Verdict.VIOLATED)

    # Sample k-size subsets
    total_subsets = comb(len(atoms_with_shards), threshold)
    exhaustive = total_subsets <= sample_size
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    if exhaustive:
        subsets = [
            list(s)
            for s in combinations(atoms_with_shards, threshold)
        ]
    else:
        subsets = [
            rng.sample(atoms_with_shards, threshold)
            for _ in range(sample_size)
        ]

    successes = sum(
        1 for subset in subsets
        if verify_holographic_reconstruction(molecule, subset)[0]
    )

    confidence = successes / len(subsets) if subsets else 0.0
    verdict = (Verdict.VERIFIED if successes == len(subsets)
               else Verdict.VIOLATED)
    return VerificationReport(
        verdict=verdict, confidence=confidence,
    )
```

## 6.6 CompositeMolecule — Hierarchical Decomposition

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/core/composite.py`)
**Context:** 324 lines. GF(2^8) limits holographic encoding to 255
evaluation points. Documents exceeding this are decomposed into
sub-molecules at natural structural boundaries, each with independent
holographic encoding. Inter-molecule bonds preserve cross-section
relationships. The composite preserves all five FATIMA properties
at both levels.

```python
"""
Composite Molecule — hierarchical decomposition for large documents.

GF(2^8) limits encoding to 255 points per molecule.
Documents exceeding this are decomposed into sub-molecules
at natural structural boundaries, each independently encoded.
"""

@dataclass
class InterMoleculeBond:
    """A bond connecting atoms in different sub-molecules."""
    source_molecule: str
    source_atom: str
    target_molecule: str
    target_atom: str
    bond_type: BondType
    weight: float = 0.8

@dataclass
class CompositeMolecule:
    composite_id: str
    sub_molecules: dict[str, Molecule] = field(default_factory=dict)
    inter_bonds: dict[str, InterMoleculeBond] = field(
        default_factory=dict
    )
    molecule_order: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def is_connected(self) -> bool:
        """All sub-molecules linked through inter-bonds.
        A disconnected composite violates Tawhidic Unity."""
        if self.sub_molecule_count <= 1: return True
        adj = {mid: set() for mid in self.sub_molecules}
        for ib in self.inter_bonds.values():
            adj[ib.source_molecule].add(ib.target_molecule)
            adj[ib.target_molecule].add(ib.source_molecule)
        visited = set()
        stack = [self.molecule_order[0]]
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            if node in visited: continue
            visited.add(node)
            stack.extend(adj[node] - visited)
        return len(visited) == self.sub_molecule_count

    def compute_composite_hash(self) -> str:
        """SHA-256 of all sub-molecule hashes + inter-bonds."""
        parts = []
        for mid in self.molecule_order:
            mol = self.sub_molecules[mid]
            parts.append(f"sub:{mid}:{mol.bond_graph_hash}")
        for bid in sorted(self.inter_bonds.keys()):
            ib = self.inter_bonds[bid]
            parts.append(
                f"inter:{ib.source_molecule}:{ib.source_atom}:"
                f"{ib.target_molecule}:{ib.target_atom}:"
                f"{ib.bond_type.value}:{ib.weight}"
            )
        material = "\n".join(parts)
        self.composite_hash = hashlib.sha256(
            material.encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()
        return self.composite_hash
```

## 6.7 CLI — The Interface

**Date:** October 2026
**Source:** fatima-core repository (`fatima/cli.py`)
**Context:** 347 lines. Three commands: encode, verify, inspect.
The encode command produces .fatima files; verify runs all five
levels; inspect prints structural summaries. The entry point
is registered in pyproject.toml as `fatima = "fatima.cli:main"`.

```python
"""
FATIMA CLI — encode, verify, and inspect .fatima files.

Usage:
  fatima encode  <input>  [--output <path>] [--title <title>]
  fatima verify  <input>  [--sample-size <n>] [--seed <n>]
  fatima inspect <input>
"""

import argparse, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="fatima",
        description="FATIMA — Fitrah-Aligned Tawhidic Integrity "
                    "for Meaning and Authenticity",
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    # encode
    enc = subparsers.add_parser("encode")
    enc.add_argument("input")
    enc.add_argument("-o", "--output")
    enc.add_argument("-t", "--title", default="")
    enc.add_argument("--ratio", type=float, default=0.5)

    # verify
    ver = subparsers.add_parser("verify")
    ver.add_argument("input")
    ver.add_argument("--sample-size", type=int, default=20)
    ver.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=None)

    # inspect
    ins = subparsers.add_parser("inspect")
    ins.add_argument("input")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "encode":
        return cmd_encode(args)
    elif args.command == "verify":
        return cmd_verify(args)
    elif args.command == "inspect":
        return cmd_inspect(args)

def cmd_verify(args):
    """Run all five verification levels."""
    structure, meta = load_fatima(Path(args.input))

    if isinstance(structure, CompositeMolecule):
        result = verify_composite(
            structure,
            holographic_sample_size=args.sample_size,
            holographic_seed=args.seed,
        )
        print(result.summary())
        return 0 if result.overall.verdict == Verdict.VERIFIED else 1

    # Single molecule: five levels
    for name, fn in [
        ("L1 Syntactic", verify_syntactic),
        ("L2 Structural", verify_structural),
    ]:
        r = fn(structure)
        _print_level(name, r)

    r = verify_holographic(
        structure, sample_size=args.sample_size, seed=args.seed
    )
    _print_level("L3 Holographic", r)

    r = verify_fitrah_alignment(structure)
    _print_level("L4 Fitrah", r)

    r = verify_authenticity(structure)
    _print_level("L5 Authenticity", r)

    return 0 if r.verdict == Verdict.VERIFIED else 1
```
